what_happened: On a multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard for no reason after handoff (17 to 8 m/s, with the lead car 19–21 m ahead), falling about 7 m behind where the human drove. It then drifted left toward the adjacent lane, and its front corner struck actor 1, a replayed car that was now beside it and slightly ahead on the left (a car behind also hit the ego's rear because of the hard braking).

After the 4.6s handoff on the highway, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (17 to 8 m/s while the gap to lead car 18 kept growing) and veered left toward the adjacent lane. Its front-left hit actor 1, which was travelling beside it in that lane. The hard braking also got the ego rear-ended, but the front collision came first.

After handoff at 4.6 s on a straight multi-lane highway, the policy braked hard for no visible reason (16.9 to 8.0 m/s while the lead car stayed about 20 m ahead) and steered left into the next lane, where its front hit car 1 alongside at 6.3 s. The route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, so the move left was the policy's own. The later rear contact was probably caused by the needless hard braking.

On a straight multi-lane highway, after handoff the ego braked hard from about 20 to 11.6 m/s with no close lead (gap about 19 m and growing). It also drifted about 1 m left of the recorded path, across its lane line, and side-swiped actor 1 in the adjacent left lane. The sudden braking probably also caused the rear contact, which came after the side collision.

On a multi-lane highway, the policy steered the ego left of the recorded path (orange plan bending left), drifting about 1.3 m toward the adjacent left lane while slowing from 6.8 to 4.4 m/s. A white pickup (actor 41) was passing on the left, and the ego's front-left corner struck it as it drew alongside. The recorded human stayed in its lane to the right.

Commanded LEFT on a left-curving road, the ego didn't follow the curve and kept going nearly straight along the right curb, 15.7 m off the human path, toward parked cars 54 and 58. It barely slowed (11.3 to 10.7 m/s) as the gap to car 54 closed from 14.8 m to 9.2 m and hit it with its front.

On a straight multi-lane highway (route command STRAIGHT, then RIGHT), the policy's planned path kept bending left out of its lane. The ego drifted left, about 1.3 m off the recorded human path, and its front hit actor 41, which was travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego slowed from about 6.8 to 4.5 m/s. Its planned path then bent left even though the command was STRAIGHT and later RIGHT. The ego crossed toward the left lane line about 1.3 m left of the recorded human path, and its front clipped actor 41, which was passing on the left.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego's planned path (orange) bent left away from the route (green). The ego drifted left into the next lane and its front hit actor 41, which was driving alongside in that lane, even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. The lead vehicle stayed 17–21 m ahead the whole time, so braking for it was not the issue.

The ego was approaching an intersection at about 17–20 m/s with a RIGHT route command and no lead vehicle. Instead of moving right with the planned path, it drifted left and ran onto the nose of the median island (a sign is right beside the car at 7.2 s), about 5 m off the recorded trajectory.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path curved right, but the policy held a straight-to-left heading at about 5–6 m/s. It cut diagonally across the lanes, away from the recorded path, and left the drivable area at 9.7s, 13 m from where the human drove. The camera was still mostly clean at 7.7s, when the ego had already moved off the path. The heavy smearing at 8.7s and 9.7s came after the drift, as the ego got far from the recorded drive, so it doesn't explain the mistake.

The route command switched to RIGHT and the recorded path bore right into the right-hand lanes at a split. The policy kept driving straight while slowing from about 21 to 16 m/s, ran onto the nose of the raised median between the two branches and left the drivable area 4.8 m from the recorded path. No actor was ahead, and the camera view was clean until the ego was on the median.

The road splits ahead and the route command changed to RIGHT, but the ego kept going straight and drifted left at about 17 m/s. It ended up about 5 m off the human's path, on the nose of the median island by the sign, and was flagged offroad. The metrics table shows no front or side collision, only offroad; the rear contact flag is incidental.

The route command switched to RIGHT. The human driver bore right into the right-hand lanes at the fork. The ego instead held a straight path at about 17–20 m/s and ran onto the island at the split, where the camera shows a sign post right in front of it. It went off-road about 5 m from the recorded path.

The route command was RIGHT, but on a multi-lane freeway the ego steered left after handoff, crossing out of its lane, about 4.9 m off the recorded path. It moved into the next lane to the left and hit vehicle 28 there with its front at about 7 m/s.

Although the route command was RIGHT, the policy steered the ego left, out of its lane and off the recorded path (4.85 m off at impact). Moving into the left lane, its front struck vehicle 28, which was coming up alongside in that lane.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego slowed from 11 to 7 m/s and drifted left, away from the recorded path, until it was 4.9 m off it and crossing into the lane on its left. There it hit actor 28, which was driving in that lane next to the ego's left-front corner.

With the route command RIGHT, the policy planned and drove a path curving left across several lanes, away from the recorded path that went right. It kept going at about 5–6 m/s until it left the drivable area 13 m from the recorded path, without hitting anything. The camera was only mildly smeared before the error, and it broke up badly only after the ego was far off the recording.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path bent right, but the policy planned and steered left across the lanes. The ego slowed to about 5 m/s and was rear-ended around 8.7 s, then kept going left until it left the drivable area at 9.7 s, about 13 m off the recorded trajectory. The rear contact did not push it off the road; its own steering did.

The command was RIGHT and the route (green line) ran off to the ego's right, but after handoff the policy angled across a multi-lane road, with its plan at 8.2s bending left away from the route. By 10.2s it had drifted 13.5 m from the recorded human path and run off the drivable area while slowly swinging back right. The camera was badly smeared, but mostly because the ego was already far from where the real car drove; the drift came first.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego's own plan held left and drifted across the yellow edge line onto the left shoulder by the guardrail, going offroad at 11.7s at about 14 m/s. Earlier, at 10.7s, replayed actor 91 clipped the ego's rear-right while passing on the right, but that contact didn't cause the drift. The camera view was mostly clear before the departure, with the yellow line plainly visible.

On a multi-lane highway with a RIGHT route command, the policy's planned path (orange) kept drifting left of the recorded path, which bore slightly right. At about 4.5 m/s the ego crossed the leftmost lane line toward the concrete median barrier and was flagged offroad at 8.9 s, 3.7 m from the human trajectory, with no other actor involved.
